clue.text: "Hit back!" Lady not content to stop at home (president's a well-known player)

indicators.note: back says the word for hit is read from right to left

parts.note: to ram is to hit

indicators.note: the pared-down lady is put in to stop up, or plug, the word for at home

parts.note: someone at home is in

indicators.note: a lady not content has lost everything inside, leaving only her outside letters

parts.note: James Monroe was the fifth US president

explanation.surface: An angry woman tells someone to retaliate, refusing to stay home, while a parenthesis praises a famous performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for hit; 'not content' strips Lady to its outer letters, which 'to stop' plugs into the word for at home, splitting it.
explanation.definitionFit: She was one of the most famous film actresses of the twentieth century, and an actor is a player.

clue.text: Plaything may come out for entertainment

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so the scrambled letters hold the other piece
out suggests the letters of come are disordered

parts.note: may and can both express permission

explanation.surface: A toy might be brought out to amuse people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the letters of come, and 'for entertainment' has them take in the word for may, as a host entertains a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a British construction toy of metal strips, nuts and bolts, so a child's plaything.

clue.text: Undoing belt I ran in and out

indicators.note: to belt is to hit or batter, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loses their trousers after dashing in and out in a hurry with a loose belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' is the anagram signal, though it looks like the trousers' strap; the letters of I RAN IN and OUT give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's undoing is the thing that ruins them, so both nouns name downfall or destruction.

clue.text: Mainly stop mentioning second romance

indicators.note: mentioning means the words are taken as heard when spoken

parts.note: a romance is a fanciful untruth, a lie, so a second one is lie two

explanation.surface: Someone half-stops talking about their second love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' means on the main, at sea, not 'mostly'; a ship that lies to stops with its head to the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing, to lie to is to stay stationary, a nautical sense of halting, hence a stop at sea.

clue.text: eSport? No

parts.note: an internet game might be called a ... game, but this one is played on a court, not online

explanation.walkthrough: The 'e' prefix suggests something online; the game's name splits into net plus ball, yet it is a real outdoor sport.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a court team game, popular with British schoolgirls, in which players shoot a ball through a high hoop.

clue.text: See 1
Lie was unravelling through leader previously not paying attention

indicators.note: the former leader's name runs through, around, the scrambled letters

parts.note: Theresa May was a former UK prime minister

indicators.note: something unravelling comes apart, so these letters lose their order

explanation.surface: A former leader's lie came apart while nobody was listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelling' scrambles LIE WAS, and 'through' sets the former leader's name around it. Theresa May was Britain's prime minister until 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone said to be daydreaming far off is distracted, an idiom for inattention.

clue.text: Divine female close to announcing a date

indicators.note: announcing means the word is said out loud

parts.note: close means near, or nigh

explanation.surface: A goddess is about to proclaim the date of an event.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is a water nymph, a minor goddess of springs and rivers.

clue.text: Going to arouse, picked up when it's not so busy

parts.note: someone going away is off

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as by a radio receiver

parts.note: to pique is to arouse interest or resentment

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to stir things up, noticed at a quiet time.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel or power use outside the rush hours is in the quieter, cheaper period of the day.

clue.text: Bill starts to complain instantly about teeth — sharp, maybe?

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: starts to picks out the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: dental means relating to teeth

explanation.surface: A patient complains at once about a dentist's bill, perhaps a steep one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp' is not keen or pricey: in music it is a note symbol written beside a note outside the key.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a sharp, flat or natural sign placed before a note is an example of this notation term.

clue.text: Doubtful Jack's missed moment

indicators.note: missed means left out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: Jack is unsure, having missed his moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something dodgy or uncertain is questionable, the colloquial synonym.

clue.text: A little crass when one eggs on lover

indicators.note: a little of the word means just its first letter

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
ova are eggs

explanation.surface: A slightly crude partner urges on a would-be romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eggs on' looks like a verb meaning encourages; it is OVA, with 'on' placing it after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian adventurer's name has become a byword for a womanising seducer.

clue.text: Nice here at office and unexpected

parts.note: Nice lies in the south of France, and sud is the French for south
a den is a study or private office

explanation.surface: A pleasant surprise awaits at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something happening abruptly, without warning.

clue.text: "Dress nice and silky," woman remarked in turn

definitions.note: spoken, 'in turn' sounds like intern, her White House job

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or set in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman takes her turn to comment on how lovely and silky a dress is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' is the anagram signal, slyly recalling her famous blue dress; NICE, SILKY and WOMAN give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the White House intern in the Clinton scandal, so a spoken 'in turn' points at her job title.

clue.text: "Right, included with promotion, you mean?" lowering head with difficulty

indicators.note: included means held inside, so the first piece holds the letter

parts.note: an ad promotes something
U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: in a down clue the opening letter is moved further down the word

parts.note: lousy means mean or rotten

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a promotion comes with a right, while hanging their head despondently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowering head' moves the L of LOUSY down to give OUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something laboriously and with great effort is the adverbial sense of hard toil.

clue.text: See 12
"Different class" — describing leader of Laura Ashley's team

parts.note: something new is different

indicators.note: to describe is to draw around, so this word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a caste is a social class

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter

explanation.surface: A fashion review praises Laura Ashley's range as being in a different class.
explanation.walkthrough: Laura Ashley is a fashion brand, but the Ashley here is Mike Ashley, who then owned Newcastle United football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club was owned by businessman Mike Ashley, so it was his side.

clue.text: Carrying racket I hurry round island

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the whole is read backwards
carrying means holding inside, so one piece contains the others

parts.note: to dart is to hurry
a din is a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a tennis racket rushes round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' puts the noise and I inside the word for hurry, and 'round' then turns the whole assembly backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the larger island of the Caribbean nation it shares with Tobago.

clue.text: Seek to cut cost of hiring dress

indicators.note: one word cuts into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: rent is the cost of hiring something
to aim is to seek or try

explanation.surface: Someone tries to lower the price of renting an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old literary word for clothing, so a synonym for garments or attire.

clue.text: Beat famous horse not on medicine

indicators.note: not means the following word is left out

parts.note: Red Rum won Britain's Grand National steeplechase three times
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A celebrated racehorse was beaten without being on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is the famous racehorse; removing RE leaves D RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat, as a past tense, means struck repeatedly, like a drum tapped by fingers.

clue.text: Kenya winger keeps changing direction

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A Kenyan footballer on the wing keeps switching flanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or plane turning about its vertical axis is veering off course.

clue.text: No, love, isn't unseemly (getting ideas)

indicators.note: unseemly means improper, so these letters behave out of order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: Someone protests that love isn't indecent, getting the wrong impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions and ideas are both thoughts or concepts, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Wish to have Congress in the same place — look out!

indicators.note: the exclamation's letters lie out, outside the other piece

parts.note: lo means look
ibid is the Latin abbreviation meaning in the same place

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out when Congress meets in the same location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the US legislature but here means sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual desire is the urge for intercourse, an old sense of congress.

clue.text: Suffer having been eaten by dog?

parts.note: something eaten is then in the eater
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Something suffers having been swallowed by a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about something unpleasant on oneself, such as a cost or penalty, is to suffer it.

clue.text: Speaker's not pursued with sexual intentions

indicators.note: a speaker's version is how it sounds out loud

parts.note: something not chased is unchased

explanation.surface: The Speaker's not being chased by someone with lustful designs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking chastity, someone lewd or immoral has carnal designs.

clue.text: Commander has only short organ

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer

indicators.note: short means a letter is cut from the end

parts.note: lone means sole, only

explanation.surface: A commanding officer has a rather small instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The large intestine is an internal body part, an example of an organ.

clue.text: Posh motor trader gets fifty per cent off

indicators.note: fifty per cent off means half the word is cut away, its back four letters

parts.note: a merchant is a trader

explanation.surface: A posh car dealer sells at half price.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mercedes-Benz is a luxury car, and this is its informal short name.

clue.text: Excitement lacking the first time? That's dissembling …

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: stimulation is excitement
T is short for time, and only the first such letter goes

explanation.surface: Faking it the first time, without real excitement, is pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for excitement contains two Ts; 'the first' says which one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigning or pretending is putting on a false show, the sense of dissembling.

clue.text: … and lies — though maybe not hers

parts.note: the surname, if ..., that is shaken up, rearranges into these two words

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: pretence and lies, though perhaps not by her.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the name as wordplay: the first word is an anagram signal acting on the surname, which yields 'and lies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult film actress claimed an affair with Donald Trump; the lies in that story were, she said, someone else's.

clue.text: See 27
